fixer.title: agentHost: use session-owned Copilot Connector accounts

introducer.title: chat: Add Copilot connectors as an authenticated customization source

cases.mechanism: Ordinary GitHub.com Connector token rotation was treated as client-level authentication, scheduling a shared Copilot runtime restart. Restart safety deferred teardown until every active turn/subagent completed, while subsequent session acquisition waited on the pending restart waiter, coupling new chat creation/restoration to unrelated long-running chats and then incurring subprocess teardown/startup.
cases.symptom: After GitHub.com token rotation, opening or restoring another Agent Host chat could remain blocked for the lifetime of an unrelated busy chat, followed by shared runtime restart latency.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed branch leaves clientAuthenticationReason undefined for GitHub.com, supplies credentials in each SDK session, and updates live static-token sessions without restarting the shared CopilotClient. New create/restore work therefore no longer waits for an unrelated busy chat or pays subprocess teardown/startup solely for Connector token rotation; Enterprise and credential-mode changes retain the deferred restart path.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, GitHub.com token changes with Connectors enabled set clientAuthenticationReason to 'Copilot Connector authentication updated', making restartRequired true and calling _requestClientRestart. That method parks the restart while any chat has in-flight work; _ensureClientForSession then loops and awaits _pendingClientRestartWaiter, so creating or restoring another session is blocked until the unrelated busy chat ends and the shared runtime is stopped. The added create/restore test at copilotAgent.test.ts:10310-10406 exercises this exact busy-chat path and asserts zero client stops plus immediate session launch after rotation.
